items.stem: The ability to read ____ is a threshold requirement of anyone who wishes to work as ____ in the excavation, all the more so ____ .

simple inscriptions in ancient Hebrew / one of the senior archaeologists / the knowledge of additional ancient languages
items.explanation: "All the more so" must lead from the less demanding post to a more demanding one: a basic skill is required of an assistant, all the more so of the manager of the excavation. (2) reverses the direction; (1) and (4) put after "all the more so" a harder skill, which does not follow from a basic requirement.

items.stem: The engineer Tzuriel ____ when he heard of the ____ results of the first year of the irrigation project in the valley, since he was convinced that the results would have been completely different had the planning committee not ____ the plan that he had submitted to it.
options: was sorry but not surprised / poor / rejected
took pride in his part in it / surprisingly good / shelved
did not feel any regret / disappointing / adopted
was angry at the committee / excellent / adopted
items.explanation: The committee rejected his plan and the results were poor, so he is sorry but not surprised. In (2) he believes that his shelved plan would have changed good results, so he has no part to be proud of; in (3) he believes that his own plan caused the disappointing results, so "no regret" does not fit; in (4) his plan was adopted and the results were excellent, so there is no reason for anger.

items.stem: In the language of the Nadali tribe, the word “orem”, which is derived from the verb “to love”, originally described a person who ____ ; ____ , today it describes mainly a person whose work is ____ .
options: earned his living from his craft / similarly / of a lower level than that of a professional
lacked skill and experience / similarly / of a high level
did something only for his own pleasure / therefore / of a high professional level
engaged in an activity out of love for it / however / of a lower level than that of a professional
items.explanation: The origin in “to love” fits a person who acts out of love, and the present meaning is different, so a contrast word is needed. In (1) and (2) "similarly" joins two meanings that are not similar, and neither fits the origin; in (3) a high professional level does not follow from doing something for pleasure.

items.stem: The new menu at Dalia's restaurant has had great success. Had its dishes been ____ , its fate would probably have been ____ the fate of her first menu, which was removed after a month, because its dishes ____ .
options: milder / similar to / were too hot even for lovers of spicy food
spicier / similar to / were too hot even for lovers of spicy food
spicier / different from / were too hot even for lovers of spicy food
milder / different from / had almost no taste
items.explanation: The first menu failed because it was too hot; a spicier new menu would have come closer to it and probably shared its fate. In (1) a milder menu moves away from the too hot menu, yet its fate is said to be similar; in (3) a spicier menu moves toward it, yet its fate is said to be different; in (4) a milder menu moves toward the tasteless one, and "different" would also mean that the successful menu actually shared the fate of a menu that failed.

items.stem: When Erez told the guide that he intended to go down to the spring by himself, the guide ____ , and explained: “____ the path to the spring ____ , and therefore ____ .”
options: tried to talk him out of it / Even those who know / lose their way on it in the dark / you should wait for the group
agreed at once / Only those who do not know / lose their way on it / it is worth your while to wait for the group and to go down together with it
tried to talk him out of it / Whoever has walked / once never forgets it / you have nothing to fear
did not object / Many who went down alone on / were hurt / it is better that you go down alone
items.explanation: The guide's explanation and conclusion must support his reaction: even experienced walkers get lost, so Erez should wait, which is why the guide tried to stop him. In (2) the guide agrees, yet ends by telling Erez to wait; in (3) the explanation removes any reason to stop him; in (4) the danger of going alone leads to advice to go alone.

items.stem: During the ____ that struck the coastal town last week ____ , and a number of visitors who, to their bad luck, were staying in the town at that time ____ .

storm / the roofs of many houses were torn off / were hurt as well

items.stem: Many companies try to prevent their workers from knowing what salaries are paid for similar work in other companies. The managements fear that workers who find out that others earn more will be dissatisfied, will lose their motivation and will blame the management. This was also the policy of the management of a large textile factory that a researcher examined. Despite the efforts of the management, a salary survey of the whole industry reached the workers of some of the factory's departments. ____ .
options: Following this, the managers were not surprised to discover that the anger toward the management had grown in the departments that had not seen the survey.
However, the great anger that arose in the departments that had seen the survey did not bring the management to understand that there is no danger at all in letting workers see such information.
Contrary to the fears of the management, it turned out that the workers in the departments that had seen the survey were more satisfied with their salary than the workers in the other departments.
As the management had expected, the workers who had seen the survey tended less than the other workers to blame the management for their low salary.
items.explanation: The paragraph prepares a result about the departments that saw the survey, and a favorable result is "contrary to" the management's fears. (1) speaks of the departments that did not see it; in (2) great anger is presented as a reason to see no danger; in (4) the management expected blame, not less blame.

items.stem: Translating the old diary from Yiddish into Hebrew was a ____ task than the translator had expected: the many words from the local dialect ____ , and ____ she found that replacing them with ordinary Hebrew words ____ .
options: harder / were explained in a list that the writer himself had left / therefore / was quick
easier / had to be looked up one by one in old dictionaries / yet / made many parts of the text difficult to understand
harder / slowed down her work / in addition / took from the diary the uniqueness of the writer's language
easier / had already been translated by an earlier researcher / nevertheless / was almost never necessary
items.explanation: The task was harder than expected: the dialect words slowed her down, and in addition replacing them spoiled the writer's language. In (1) everything described makes the work easier, not harder; in (2) the difficulties do not fit an easier task; in (4) "nevertheless" joins two facts that both make the work easier.

items.stem: The cleaning material that Galit has been using for years contains a substance that ____ the thin layer that protects marble floors. Galit's floor is made of marble, whereas the floor in the house of her neighbor Bella, who uses the same material, is made of a stone that ____ such a protective layer. Therefore, ____ that ____ .
options: strengthens / does not need / it is not surprising / Galit's floor lost its shine, while Bella's floor stayed as it was
wears away / does not need / it is not surprising / only Galit's floor lost its shine over the years
wears away / does not need / it is strange / Galit's floor was damaged and Bella's was not
protects / also has / it is not surprising / both floors were damaged to the same degree
items.explanation: The substance wears away the layer that only marble needs, so it is to be expected that only Galit's marble floor was damaged. In (1) a substance that strengthens the layer is not expected to dull the floor; in (3) the expected result is called strange; in (4) a substance that protects the layer is not expected to damage both floors.

items.stem: The critic Ben-Ami ____ that the audience always responded to the works of the choreographer Barak with ____ , since such a reaction is not ____ at performances of experimental dance. The rest of the critics, in contrast to the audience, tended ____ these works.
options: was surprised / enthusiasm / common / to criticize
was surprised / angry protest / rare / to praise
was surprised / great admiration / common / to praise
was not surprised / enthusiastic applause / common / to reject
items.explanation: The enthusiasm is surprising at experimental works, and the critics, "in contrast to the audience", criticize. In (2) a reaction that is not rare is called surprising; in (3) the critics praise the works, like the audience; in (4) an uncommon reaction is not surprising.

items.stem: When the writer Gil discovered that the date for handing in the manuscript to the publisher ____ , he felt ____ , since ____ .
options: had been brought forward by a week / relief / he had not yet begun to write the last chapter
had been put off by a month / disappointment / he was in no hurry to finish the book
had not changed / great anxiety / he had finished the book a month before
had been put off by a month / relief / two chapters were still not written
items.explanation: A later date with two chapters still unwritten is a reason for relief. In (1) an earlier date is a relief although the last chapter is not begun; in (2) a postponement disappoints someone in no hurry; in (3) a writer who finished a month before has no reason for anxiety.

items.stem: The forecast that the number of students at a certain college would ____ during the last decade ____ : ____ in the tuition fees at the college, ____ the number of students who continued until the end of their studies.

shrink / did not come true / despite the rise / the enrollment of new students rose in those years, and so did
shrink / came true / despite the rise / the number of students who dropped out rose in those years, and likewise there was a drop in
grow / did not come true / partly because of the rise / the number of students who dropped out rose in those years, but in those same years there was a sharp rise in
items.explanation: Despite higher fees, which would suggest shrinking, both enrollment and completion rose, so the forecast did not come true. items.stem: The philosophers Amitai and Harpaz hold opposing positions regarding the place of reason in the actions of man: ____ holds that reason alone can determine what a person must do, whereas ____ holds that reason is subordinate to the feelings. “____ agree with Harpaz,” said the lecturer, “because ____ in most cases the feelings are ____ than reason in determining the way in which people act.”
options: Harpaz / Amitai / I / it is wrong to claim that / weaker
Amitai / Harpaz / I do not / it seems to me that / stronger
Amitai / Harpaz / I / it seems to me that / stronger
Harpaz / Amitai / I do not / it is hard to believe that / stronger
items.explanation: Harpaz holds that reason is subordinate to the feelings, so the lecturer agrees with him because feelings are stronger than reason. In each other choice the lecturer's reason supports the opposite side from the one he takes.
